chunks: And ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Muyassir, who said:
I said to him: “A man comes to me and says, ‘Will you buy for me?’ while what I have is better than the merchandise of the market.”
He said: “If you are confident that he will not suspect you, then give him from what you have; but if you fear that he may suspect you, then buy for him from the market.”

key_terms.السُّوقِ: the marketplace from which items are bought
key_terms.تَشْتَرِي: to purchase on behalf of someone else
key_terms.فَأَعْطِهِ: then give it to him from your own possession
key_terms.يَتَّهِمَكَ: to suspect or accuse you of unfair dealing

ai.seo_question: Can a person sell his own item when someone asks him to buy something on their behalf?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a ruling on acting for another person in a purchase when one already possesses a suitable item. It permits giving one's own goods if there is no fear of suspicion, but instructs purchasing from the market if mistrust may arise. The narration reflects both legal care and ethical concern for transparency in transactions.
